eligibility_reason: Original research proposing a semi-supervised bounding-box object detector (TaDP-Det, built on Faster R-CNN with ResNet-50) and evaluating it on NEU-DET and GC10-DET.

F01.value: 1800 grayscale images, 6 classes (300 per class), 200x200, Northeastern University
F01.evidence: It contains 1800 grayscale images of size 200×200, evenly distributed over six defect categories: crazing (Cr), inclusion (In), patches (Pa), pitted surface (PS), rolled-in scale (RS), and scratches (Sc), with 300 samples per class.

coder_notes: Semi-supervised object detection (SSOD) evaluated under 1%, 5%, and 10% labeled data ratios on NEU-DET (TaDP-Det mAP0.5: 53.2 / 65.6 / 71.8 vs Faster R-CNN* supervised-only: 13.0 / 41.5 / 56.7 and Mix Teacher: 45.7 / 65.3 / 70.6; SSOD teacher-student baseline in Table 5 at 10% is 65.1) and under 5% and 10% labeled ratios on GC10-DET (TaDP-Det mAP0.5: 50.2 / 58.2 vs Faster R-CNN* supervised-only: 23.4 / 34.5 and Mix Teacher: 45.9 / 55.7).
